title: TeleMom - Mixed methods study on the feasibility of telemonitoring of patients with hypertensive disorders in pregnancy (HES)
summary: Hypertensive pregnancy disorders (HES) occur in 6-8% of all pregnancies. As there is no causal therapy, treatment focuses on early detection, drug prophylaxis with low-dose aspirin and sequential outpatient presentation in specialized practices/outpatient clinics. This means that prenatal care in Germany in accordance with the Maternity Directive (Mu-RL) continues to be provided in analog form without any nationally established digital care models or programs. However, there are diagnostic gaps and deficits in the analog care process, which make informed and participatory decision-making by patients and doctors more difficult. Digitally supported care models, including the use of telemonitoring, have proven positive clinical care effects in national and international studies in various medical specialties, e.g. in the treatment of heart failure in cardiology, and have improved the safety of care. In view of the strained perinatal medical care situation in Germany, the Federal Ministry of Health is now increasingly promoting digitally supported care models, especially for pregnancy. For the study, a modular telemonitoring system was adapted to the care of HES patients based on the nationally established telemedical heart failure monitoring in cardiology. The requested qualitative study with supplementary quantitative questionnaire evaluation (mixed methods) accompanies the preparation for the establishment of the telemonitoring system at a university perinatal center.

interventions.name: Potential users of telemonitoring for hypertensive disorders in pregnancy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical professionals (midwives, doctors, nursing staff)
- Medical activity in the Perinatal Center of the University Hospital Marburg or in the Marburg-Biedenkopf care region
- Sufficient knowledge of German (> B2)

Patient representatives
- Past or current pregnancy with an HES with treatment in the Perinatal Center of the University Hospital Marburg or in the Marburg-Biedenkopf care region
- Sufficient knowledge of German (> B2)
Exclusion criteria:
- No private use of smartphones (reason: smartphones are indispensable for the use of the telemonitoring application (data acquisition, communication)).
